name: application-confirmation-input
title: Confirmation Input
description: Destructive-action dialog that requires the user to type an exact phrase, such as a resource name, before the confirm button becomes enabled.
useWhen: The action is irreversible and high-consequence, such as deleting a project, repository, or account.
You want a stronger safeguard than a single confirm click, without adding extra steps like email verification.
The item being deleted has a name or identifier the user already knows, which can double as the confirmation phrase.
avoidWhen: The action is reversible or low-consequence — a standard AlertDialog with a single confirm click is enough friction.
The user won't reliably know the exact phrase to type (e.g. a long UUID) — offer a copy-to-clipboard affordance or a simpler checkbox confirmation instead.
The action needs multi-factor or server-side re-authentication — this component only gates the button locally, it isn't a security boundary.
responsiveBehavior: The dialog is a fixed max-w-sm card that centers in its container at all viewport widths.
accessibility: Uses role="alertdialog" with aria-labelledby and aria-describedby so assistive tech announces the destructive context immediately.
The confirm button uses the native disabled attribute, not just a visual style, so it's unreachable by keyboard and unannounced as actionable until the phrase matches.
The input's aria-describedby always points at either the disabled-state hint or the confirmed-state message, kept in sync with the visual border color change.

variants.title: Awaiting confirmation
variants.description: Dialog with an empty confirmation field and a disabled destructive confirm button.
accessibility: The confirm button is a real disabled button, not a styled-only state.

variants.title: Awaiting confirmation (Dark)
variants.description: Confirmation dialog in its disabled state, adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Disabled button and input border colors must remain distinguishable on dark surfaces.

variants.title: Confirmed
variants.description: Same dialog once the typed value matches the required phrase: input border turns success-colored and the confirm button is enabled.
accessibility: The success message is programmatically linked via aria-describedby, not conveyed by border color alone.

variants.title: Confirmed (Dark)
variants.description: Matched-phrase confirmed state adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Success-state border and text colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
